block_suggestions.name: Image triage and payload verification
block_suggestions.outcome: Choose metadata, appended-file or LSB/carrier extraction based on evidence and validate recovered bytes.
block_suggestions.diagnostic: Without notes, distinguish ExifTool metadata from zsteg pixel bits and Binwalk signatures. Explain why --seed is not a universal password bypass. If all are clear, skim docs and do the recall exercise.
block_suggestions.preparation: Save the four selected sections. Optional execution requires already installed tools, a personal JPEG with metadata, and a scratch directory; no event files required.
block_suggestions.exercise: Reading-only: use zsteg README cats.png output to identify the red-channel and green-channel one-bit text candidates and write the matching -E selector for the b1,r,lsb,xy result. From Binwalk docs, list which confidence level validates only magic bytes. From ExifTool examples, write a command retaining duplicate and unknown tags.
block_suggestions.assessment: Answers: red-channel text names Marussia; green-channel text prompts you to look deeper; extraction selector b1,r,lsb,xy; Binwalk red is low confidence; exiftool -a -u -g1 image.jpg. A reported format still needs independent validation. No supplied exercise was executed.

block_suggestions.name: Audio and stream handling
block_suggestions.outcome: Select the intended audio stream and choose a time/frequency display that answers the hypothesis.
block_suggestions.diagnostic: Explain whether a 2048-sample window improves time or frequency resolution relative to 256, and interpret -map 0:1. If both are immediate, go straight to the exercise.
block_suggestions.preparation: Save Audacity figures, FFmpeg Streamcopy and Sonic Visualiser reference. For optional GUI work, bring a personal WAV and working local Audacity or Sonic Visualiser; source audio must accompany saved sessions.
block_suggestions.exercise: Reading-only: compare the two-click and overtone pictures in Audacity. State which window separates clicks and which separates close frequencies. Draft the official FFmpeg command to copy stream index 1 from INPUT.mkv to OUTPUT.mp4, then state why filtering cannot accompany streamcopy. Optional GUI: open a personal WAV, switch between 256 and 2048, and record one visible change.
block_suggestions.assessment: Expected: 256 gives finer time resolution, 2048 finer frequency resolution; ffmpeg -i INPUT.mkv -map 0:1 -c copy OUTPUT.mp4; filters need decoded frames. Container compatibility can still prevent the copy. Exercise not executed.

block_suggestions.name: Optional self-generated steghide round trip
block_suggestions.outcome: Recover known bytes from a carrier using a tiny wordlist and check the result without AI.
block_suggestions.diagnostic: Can you state the difference between an embedding password and encryption-disabled seed recovery?
block_suggestions.preparation: Before flying, confirm approved steghide and stegseek work, bring a sufficiently large personal JPEG, create an empty scratch directory. No external wordlist required.
block_suggestions.exercise: In the scratch directory, create note.txt containing a short known phrase. Run steghide embed -cf carrier.jpg -ef note.txt -sf practice.jpg and choose a disposable known password at the prompt. Put that password and two decoys on separate lines in words.txt. Run stegseek practice.jpg words.txt recovered.txt. Compare recovered.txt byte-for-byte with note.txt using an available comparison tool or hex viewer.
block_suggestions.assessment: Success requires exact original bytes and a successful exit, not just a plausible filename. If embedding reports insufficient capacity choose a larger carrier; if an output already exists choose a fresh filename. This exercise was designed from documented syntax, not executed.

family_rationales.rationale: ZBar, xxd, file and foremost are short task-driven identification/conversion/carving lookups. They support triage but do not each justify another long lesson; keep each existing reference and consult it when QR, hex, unknown-format or carving evidence appears.

Image channels and integrity remain an important reference family. zsteg does not replace visual bit-plane inspection or PNG/JPEG validation. Keep ImageMagick/G’MIC channel manipulation, StegSolve bit planes and pngcheck/jpeginfo integrity references; prioritise these on a challenge with damaged headers, CRC errors or visible channel clues. Installed fork/version remains relevant.

MediaInfo and SoX_ng overlap common inspection covered by FFmpeg/Audacity; keep reference-only to avoid repeat lessons. SSTV is a distinct narrow encoding and must remain discoverable, but the decoder-versus-PySSTV package mismatch prevents treating execution as a dependable flight prerequisite.

OpenStego-specific and SNOW whitespace extraction are recognisable narrow branches. Retain existing direct references and lookup triggers; generic PNG LSB or audio study does not imply mastery of these formats.
AperiSolve is reference-only because local deployment preparation is substantial and its analyzer set overlaps individually taught tools; public upload is forbidden for event artifacts.
Sonic Visualiser is covered by the free reading alternative and optional audio investigation, rather than a duplicate full audio-editor lesson. Its v5.2.1 reference matches the workbook version.

limitations: No audiovisual playback, tool commands or exercise execution performed. No accounts, purchases, portal launches or media collections accessed.
All study-minute recommendations are estimates; only media-8 has a retrieved published runtime.
